title: XR accessibility for low-vision users
bottleneck: XR is built for the sighted: interfaces assume good acuity, stereo vision, and precise gaze, excluding users with low vision, blindness, or binocular disorders. Audio-haptic alternatives are afterthoughts, magnification tools are crude, and vergence-accommodation conflict hits some visual conditions harder. Accessibility in 3D spatial computing lags decades behind 2D.
why_it_blocks: Excluding disabled users from the next computing platform repeats old mistakes at larger scale. If XR becomes essential infrastructure, inaccessibility becomes discrimination.
current_state: Some platforms add basic accessibility features (text scaling, audio cues), but comprehensive low-vision XR design guidelines and tooling barely exist. Spatial interfaces designed for stereo vision and precise gaze exclude users whose vision differs, with few real alternatives offered. Audio-haptic alternatives to visual UI are usually afterthoughts, so blind users get a degraded shadow of the experience.
